name: hcapp_setMultiRunRsvpAndCheckin
description: Processes the multi-run check-in dialog result in a single transaction. For each event in @checkInEventIds, upserts HasherEventMap with AttendenceState=20 (at hash) and RsvpState=3 (RSVP yes), guarded so existing check-ins (AttendenceState >= 20) are never downgraded. For each event in @rsvpNoEventIds, upserts HasherEventMap with RsvpState=1 (not coming), guarded so rows where the hasher is already checked in are not touched. Both lists are pipe-delimited UUID strings; an id with no HC.Event row is silently skipped (INNER JOIN). Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 93, device-secret token, @param NULL). There is NO permission gate: @hasherId defaults to the caller but any value is accepted. After the transaction, runs HC6.nonApi_updateRunCountsByUser for check-in events, then delegates to HC6.hcapp_syncUserData (common domain) to replicate attendance changes back to the device. Self only: @hasherId other than the caller returns errorCode 1393 / errorType 13 'Not authorised' (2026-10-13).

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Passed to HC6.ValidateAppAuth (SP number 93, auth errorCode range 1193/1393) and forwarded to hcapp_syncUserData.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived auth token validated against DeviceSecret. @param = NULL (device-secret-only auth). Also forwarded to hcapp_syncUserData.

parameters.name: checkInEventIds
parameters.description: Pipe-delimited list of event UUIDs to check in to (AttendenceState=20, RsvpState=3). Pass an empty string or NULL (the parameter has no default, so it must still be sent) to skip check-in processing. UUIDs are TRIM()ed before CAST.

parameters.name: rsvpNoEventIds
parameters.description: Pipe-delimited list of event UUIDs to mark RSVP No (RsvpState=1). Pass an empty string or NULL (the parameter has no default, so it must still be sent) to skip RSVP-No processing. Never downgrades existing check-ins.

parameters.name: hasherId
parameters.description: Target hasher to check in or RSVP for. If NULL, set to the authenticated caller (line 73). Any other hasher id is accepted WITHOUT a permission check (see codeSmells). The app always sends its own userId.

parameters.name: hasherEventMapUpdatedAfter
parameters.description: Sync watermark forwarded to hcapp_syncUserData for the HasherEventMap rowset. Pass 'ignore' to skip that domain. No default — must be sent; a NULL value is COALESCE'd to 'ignore'.

parameters.name: hasherKennelMapUpdatedAfter
parameters.description: Sync watermark forwarded to hcapp_syncUserData for the HasherKennelMap rowset. Pass 'ignore' to skip that domain. No default — must be sent; a NULL value is COALESCE'd to 'ignore'.

rowsets.name: Envelope
rowsets.description: Always returned as rowset 0. success=0 on auth failure (ValidateAppAuth codes) or unhandled error (1993 / errorType 19); success=1 on success (errorCode/errorType NULL).

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: NULL on success. Auth error codes (1193/1393) or CATCH error code (1993).

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: NULL on success. 1=auth, 3=device not found, 19=unhandled CATCH error.

rowsets.name: ErrorDetail
rowsets.description: Returned at rowset 1 when success=0. Standard HC6 app error shape. Mutually exclusive with AdHocData and sync rowsets.

rowsets.name: AdHocData
rowsets.description: Returned at rowset 1 when success=1. Minimal confirmation token per the adHocDataId pattern. Mutually exclusive with ErrorDetail rowset.

columns.name: adHocDataId
columns.description: Always 1. Sentinel value confirming successful write. Clients should check rowset 0 success=1 rather than inspecting this value.

rowsets.name: SyncUserDataRowsets
rowsets.description: Rowsets 2+ are the output of HC6.hcapp_syncUserData (common domain) called with @hashersUpdatedAfter='ignore', the caller-supplied HEM and HKM watermarks. The exact rowset count and shapes match hcapp_syncUserData's contract. Only present when success=1.

rowsets.name: NotAuthorisedError
rowsets.description: Returned when the caller may not act for @hasherId: rowset 0 {success 0, errorCode 1393, errorType 13}, rowset 1 {errorId, errorType, errorCode, errorTitle, errorUserMessage, errorProc}. Logged to HC.ErrorLog before return; no transaction is open.

sideEffects: Upserts HC.HasherEventMap rows for all event UUIDs in @checkInEventIds (AttendenceState=20, RsvpState=3). Guard: never downgrades AttendenceState >= 20.
Upserts HC.HasherEventMap rows for all event UUIDs in @rsvpNoEventIds (RsvpState=1). Guard: never touches rows where AttendenceState >= 20.

Calls HC6.nonApi_updateRunCountsByUser(@hasherId) after commit if @checkInEventIds is non-empty — best-effort, wrapped in TRY/CATCH so a failure logs to HC.ErrorLog but does not surface as a SP error.
Calls HC6.hcapp_syncUserData with common-domain watermarks to return updated HEM and HKM data.
Writes to HC.ErrorLog on auth failure (via ValidateAppAuth) and on CATCH error.

codeSmells.detail: All seven parameters (@deviceId, @accessToken, @checkInEventIds, @rsvpNoEventIds, @hasherId, @hasherEventMapUpdatedAfter, @hasherKennelMapUpdatedAfter) (lines 3-9) have no SQL default. A client that omits one is refused by SQL before the procedure runs: no HC.ErrorLog row, an empty 500 in the app, and any graceful check inside is unreachable (CLAUDE.md, Rack of Lamb 2026-09-29).
Line 131 uses errorType=19 / errorCode 1993, not the standard 5 for unhandled errors. Callers that branch on errorType 5 miss this case.

codeSmells.issue: No validation on malformed event UUID strings
codeSmells.detail: Lines 84/108: CAST(TRIM(s.value) AS UNIQUEIDENTIFIER) throws on a non-GUID segment; the CATCH logs a raw conversion error with no hint which id was bad. Ids that are valid GUIDs but match no HC.Event are dropped silently by the INNER JOIN.

Lines 94/99/117/122 write GETDATE() (server local time) rather than SYSUTCDATETIME()/SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(). The HasherEventMap UpdatedAt trigger restamps the row, so the literal is redundant and misleading.

codeSmells.issue: RSVP-No MERGE can fire for a run the hasher already has a row for at state >= 20
codeSmells.detail: By design the WHEN MATCHED guard (line 114) skips checked-in rows, so a No for an attended run is silently ignored and the client still receives success=1.

breakingChanges: Pipe delimiter (|) for event UUID lists is project-standard. Callers must never use comma-delimited lists.
hcapp_syncUserData is called with @hashersUpdatedAfter='ignore' hardcoded — the Hashers rowset is never included in the sync response from this SP regardless of what callers pass.
The CATCH block uses errorType=19 (non-standard). Callers should treat any success=0 at rowset 0 as an error regardless of errorType value.
